nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong sun and long dry months drive the park's dry deciduous forest, which looks brown in summer.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says the characteristic dhonk tree turns green after even a few drops of rain, so the rains set the rhythm of food in this dry forest.

nodes.name: Lakes & waterholes
nodes.desc: The park holds many lakes and streams, Padam Talao being the largest. In a dry landscape they draw grazers and the crocodiles that live in them.

nodes.name: Rocky soil
nodes.desc: The park is hilly with rocky ground and open meadows, between roughly 215 and 505 m above sea level.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria & insects
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Dhok
nodes.desc: Wikipedia calls it the characteristic tree of Ranthambore. It looks dry and brown in summer but greens up after a little rain.

nodes.name: Banyan
nodes.desc: A large fig tree whose fruit is eaten by many birds and mammals, including golden jackals in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Jamun
nodes.desc: A fruiting tree whose fruit appears in records of wild boar, golden jackals and many birds feeding on it.

nodes.name: Babul
nodes.desc: A thorny acacia of dry country. Its pods and leaves are browsed by hoofed animals such as nilgai and blackbuck.

nodes.name: Grasses & herbs
nodes.desc: Open meadows and grassy patches among the trees feed the grazing deer and antelope.

nodes.name: Sambar
nodes.desc: A large deer and one of the most-recorded mammals here. Wikipedia lists sambar as a preferred tiger prey.

nodes.name: Chital
nodes.desc: The spotted deer of the open meadows and forest edge, and the usual prey of tigers, leopards and the park's crocodiles.

nodes.name: Nilgai
nodes.desc: Asia's largest antelope. Records show tigers, leopards and striped hyenas feeding on it.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that digs for roots and eats fruit, and a medium-sized prey of tigers and leopards.

nodes.name: Northern plains gray langur
nodes.desc: A leaf-and-fruit-eating monkey that is regular prey for tigers and leopards and sometimes for crocodiles.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Build mounds and recycle dry grass and wood. They are the main food of sloth bears.

nodes.name: Sloth bear
nodes.desc: Eats mainly termites, ants and bees, plus fruit; fruit dominates winter diets in Rajasthan's Aravalli hills. Tigers sometimes kill it.

nodes.name: Striped hyena
nodes.desc: A shy scavenger of the dry forest that cleans up carcasses left by tigers and leopards.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: Opportunist that eats fruit, small animals and carrion, including the remains of big-cat kills.

nodes.name: Mugger crocodile
nodes.desc: Lives in the park's lakes. It eats fish, birds and monkeys, and deer up to chital size, and scavenges.

nodes.name: Bengal monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard of dry forest and scrub that eats insects and small animals and scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Bengal tiger
nodes.desc: Ranthambore's star animal. Numbers fell to about 15 in the early 2000s and reached 69 by 2022. It hunts sambar, chital, nilgai and boar.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: Smaller than the tiger and more of a generalist, taking chital, sambar, boar, langurs and jackals, though tigers sometimes kill leopards.
